chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The people of Syria are more evil than the people of Rome, and the people of Medina are more evil than the people of Mecca, and the people of Mecca disbelieve in Allah openly.
ai.seo_question: What is the comparative spiritual status of the people of Syria, Rome, Medina, and Mecca according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a comparative eschatological and moral ranking of key Islamic communities, highlighting the severity of the people of Syria and Medina relative to their counterparts. The specific mention of the people of Mecca declaring disbelief openly (*bi-jahra*) reflects the historical context of the Umayyad and Abbasid eras, where political power often coexisted with outward piety, whereas Mecca's elite were noted for their explicit rejection of divine authority. This evaluation serves to distinguish between different types of adversaries and spiritual decay within the broader Muslim ummah.
